section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of the current study, which investigated the role of creativity in mate selection, specifically differentiating between ornamental/aesthetic and applied/technological forms of creativity. The study found that ornamental/aesthetic creativity was considered more sexually attractive for both males and females. Individual differences in mate preferences were predicted by personality and creative achievement, with general cognitive ability negatively predicting a preference for applied/technological creativity among males. The Creativity Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ) was used, and limitations included a sample primarily consisting of university students with restricted age and nonverbal cognitive ability ranges.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the current study's findings on the role of creativity in mate selection, highlighting that ornamental/aesthetic creativity was considered more sexually attractive than applied/technological forms. It also details how individual differences in mate preferences were predicted by personality and creative achievement, with general cognitive ability negatively predicting a preference for applied/technological creativity among males. The section connects these findings to previous research by Nusbaum and Silvia (2011), Kaufman (2013), and Feist and Barron (2003) regarding the predictive validity of Openness and Intellect on creative achievement. The authors acknowledge limitations, noting that their sample consisted primarily of university students, which restricted the range of creative achievement and nonverbal cognitive ability.
